objective: Decide whether the converged correction field from the CBFS field inversion reports where the turbulence model is wrong, or merely where the objective happens to be sensitive, by measuring the rank agreement between the final correction and the baseline adjoint sensitivity across all 21,000 cells, at zero solver compute from arrays already archived on disk
rationale: The CBFS inversion line has a passing objective gate and a failing geography gate, and the failing one has never been diagnosed. G1 passed at 0.25847, a 74.2 percent reduction against a bar of 0.70. G2 asked that more than half of the top decile of correction magnitude sit inside a pre-declared window covering the recirculation bubble, the separated shear layer and the near recovery region; it measured 26.9 percent, against an all-cells base rate of 8.4 percent. It also failed before the objective repair, at 29.0 percent, so the repair moved the objective by a factor of four and moved the geography slightly the wrong way. The window is not the suspect: the stage A loss audit re-confirmed it, finding that those same cells carry 41.2 percent of the loss while holding 8.4 percent of the cells, the largest loss concentration per cell anywhere in the domain. So the loss is concentrated inside the window and the correction is not, with 39.6 percent of the top decile sitting upstream of the step crest and 31.5 percent sitting above the shear layer. Two readings survive and nobody has separated them. Either model form error in this closure is genuinely set upstream by boundary layer history and merely expressed in the bubble, which is a physical claim worth publishing, or the inversion is depositing its correction wherever the adjoint is most sensitive, which is a statement about identifiability and not about turbulence at all. The second reading is testable today and has never been tested. The baseline gradient at a correction of unity was archived for both runs, along with the final correction, the cell centre array and the window mask, and the design variable permutation needed to align them. Nothing else on this line can be settled this cheaply, and both of the expensive successors on the S1 ladder are priced on the assumption that the first reading is the true one
gate: Three quantities, all thresholds declared here before any arithmetic runs. (1) SPEARMAN: rank correlation between |beta_final - 1| and |g_baseline| over all 21,000 cells, where g_baseline is the archived adjoint gradient at beta = 1 (grad_anchor8.npy for the reinversion at primalTol 1e-8, grad_eval001.npy for the first inversion), both mapped into serial cell order through dv_to_serial_perm.npy. (2) OVERLAP: the fraction of the 2,100-cell top decile of |beta_final - 1| that also lies in the 2,100-cell top decile of |g_baseline|; chance level is 10%. (3) NULL MODEL: the pure first-step prediction beta_pred - 1 = -alpha * g_baseline, with alpha fitted by least squares, reported with its own Spearman and overlap against the measured field. VERDICT, three-valued per docket B2. SENSITIVITY-DRIVEN if Spearman >= 0.6 AND overlap >= 40%: G2's failure is then an identifiability artefact, the 26.9% figure is not a statement about where model-form error lives, and every FIML localisation claim in this lab needs the sensitivity map published beside it. PHYSICAL if Spearman <= 0.3 AND overlap <= 15%: 26.9% stands as a measured statement about where the correction goes, and the upstream concentration becomes a research finding. UNDECIDED anywhere in between, reported as undecided and NOT forced to a side. Run on BOTH archived runs (first inversion and reinversion) and report both; a verdict that differs between them is itself the finding. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: a low correlation. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? YES, and this is the one real hazard: an inversion that barely moved would satisfy beta - 1 proportional to -g_baseline BY CONSTRUCTION from its own first gradient step, and would score a high Spearman while proving nothing. That is why the NULL MODEL leg is gated too, and why this run qualifies: it took 16 evaluations, cut the objective 74.2%, and drove the gradient norm down by a factor of 106, so the final iterate is far from a single steepest-descent step. If the measured field and the fitted first-step prediction agree to better than Spearman 0.9, the run is declared TOO CLOSE TO ITS FIRST STEP and the whole comparison is reported as inconclusive rather than as a sensitivity verdict. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: the window geometry is checked against the separation and reattachment locations of the Bentaleb, Lardeau and Leschziner (2012) large eddy simulation of this exact configuration, distributed on the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource, so the window is anchored to an independently computed flow structure rather than to our own mesh coordinates. The correlation itself has NO external referent and this proposal says so plainly: it is a statement about the relationship between two of our own archived arrays, and its value is diagnostic rather than validating.
cost_basis: Zero solver compute, and the basis for the zero is that every input was verified present on disk before this was filed: the final correction, the baseline gradient at unity, the cell centre array, the window mask, the top decile index and the design variable permutation, each 21,000 double precision entries per field, in two archived run directories. The arithmetic is two rank correlations and one least squares fit over arrays of that size, which is seconds of host time on this box. The precedent for pricing this class at zero is the plateau balance reconciliation carried out on 2026-08-11, which recomputed three published figures from two of these same archived arrays at zero solver compute and closed a disputed correction. No estimate is made by analogy to any solve, because no solve is involved
expected_knowledge_gain: This separates two readings of a published FAIL verdict that currently travels with no diagnosis at all, and it does so before any of the money that depends on the answer is spent. A SENSITIVITY-DRIVEN verdict would retire the physical interpretation of the 26.9 percent figure in two published records, and would redirect roughly 330 core minutes of already-planned reinversion work toward a preconditioned formulation rather than another unconditioned one. A PHYSICAL verdict is the stronger result of the two: it would mean the correction concentrates upstream of the region carrying the loss, which is a concrete, checkable claim about where this closure's error originates, and it would make a spatially structured prior a defensible thing to build rather than a hopeful one. An UNDECIDED verdict is also worth the price, because the price is zero and the alternative is spending on a premise nobody measured. The general form matters beyond this case: a correction field inferred by an adjoint is not automatically a map of model error, and this lab does not currently publish anything that would let a reader tell the difference
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. It is host arithmetic over arrays a completed and already-paid-for case wrote to disk, so charter 3's hardness floor governs nothing here
